title: Context Anchorization and Slot Merging: cross-request compact allocator for prefix reuse
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Problem: Requests with overlapping prefixes (shared system messages, instruction templates, or repeated user context) are causing redundant KV cache allocations on GPU memory, driving up per-GPU resident memory and increasing eviction churn. Existing prefix dedupe approaches (fingerprints and slab coalescing) reduce duplication but still produce fragmentation and repeated small allocations when similar-but-not-identical prefixes are present across sessions and tenants.

Proposal: Implement 'Context Anchorization' (CA) — a two-stage compactification + allocation strategy that: (1) normalizes prefixes into anchor segments (semantic-aware split points), (2) stores anchors in a content-addressed compact store on GPU (anchor-store), and (3) performs 'Slot Merging' at allocation time to map multiple anchored segments to contiguous GPU slots where safe. The allocator will be integrated with the continuous batching pipeline and the KV residency tracker to enable: higher cross-request reuse, lower metadata overhead, and reduced GPU fragmentation.

Key ideas: 
- Anchorization: canonicalize prompt headers/instructions by token-level normalization (whitespace/placeholder collapsing + small canonicalization map) and use similarity thresholds to split into stable anchors.
- Anchor-store: content-addressable GPU resident store with compacted slabs for hot anchors; reference-counted entries and lightweight per-anchor fingerprints (64-bit) to avoid heavy hashing costs.
- Slot Merging: when assembling a request's KV fingerprint vector, attempt to co-locate contiguous anchors into merged GPU slots if they map to adjacent slab offsets and eviction-safe boundaries, reducing pointer indirection and increasing contiguous residency.
- Residency credits & GC-driven compaction: assign credits to anchors based on hit frequency and request criticality; low-credit anchors are eligible for opportunistic compaction and eviction during low-load windows to free contiguous slots.

Why different: This combines semantic-aware canonicalization with allocation-level coalescing (not just pure dedupe), enabling significant footprint compression for common instruction templates while preserving latency SLOs via conservative merging heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation integrated with continuous batching runtime and enabled behind feature flag 'ca_slot_merge'
Measured >=15% reduction in average GPU KV-resident bytes for our benchmark set of customer-like workloads (instruction-heavy + chat) compared to baseline dedupe
No regression in P95 generation latency by more than 5ms for 95% of requests during canary
Hit-rate telemetry for anchor-store and merged slots emitted to console (per-model, per-tenant)
Canary rollout plan with automatic rollback on increased 99th-percentile tail latency or increased eviction rate
tasks: DRAFT: design doc / confluence (Aditi) - cover canonicalization rules, anchor boundary heuristics, slot-merge safety model
Prototype anchorizer in Python for offline trace replay (Marco) - evaluate split stability and collision rates
Implement anchor-store gadget in runtime C++ with 64-bit fingerprint and refcounts (eng core)
Allocator: implement slot-merge policy and contiguous-slot allocator adjustments (eng memory team)
Integrate telemetry hooks: anchor hit/miss, merge success, eviction-triggered splits (Sana)
E2E tests: synthetic workload harness + replay traces from prod-like dataset (Benji)
Canary rollout: small percentage of runtime-1.23 fleet behind feature flag with auto-metrics gate (Ops)
Design review and security checklist completion (security_review_required=false but review needed for multi-tenant invariants)
notes: 2026-03-03 - Aditi: Initial spike shows anchor collision rate ~0.6% for canonicalization map of 1,200 templates when using 64-bit fingerprints. Prototype anchorizer identifies stable split points for 87% of instruction templates.

2026-03-05 - Marco: Prototype indicates merged-slot assignments reduce slab fragmentation by ~22% on replay traces, but increases CPU allocation decision time by ~1.2ms per batch. Need to assess tradeoff for low-latency SLO customers.

2026-03-07 - Design review notes (Sana, Benji): require strict tenant isolation—merged slots must never co-reside across tenant boundaries unless flag 'allow_shared_slots' is enabled and tenant consents. Add per-tenant tenancy bit to anchor metadata.
2026-03-09 - Security (Ethan): verified that 64-bit fingerprinting is fine for dedupe but recommended salt-per-tenant to mitigate collision / fingerprint-reuse attacks; added to scope.

2026-03-10 - Marco: Built allocator prototype in C++; initial canary harness ready. Observed 18% reduction in resident KV bytes on a mixed chat+instruction trace; P95 latency unchanged on bench harness but tail latency shows rare spikes when compaction runs concurrently. Plan: throttle background compaction during active batches.

2026-03-11 - Ops (Lina): Canary scheduled for 2026-03-16 on 5% of capacity for models gpt-j-ops and rwd-4b. Monitoring dashboards created: anchor-store/hit-rate, merged-slot-utilization, compaction-ops/sec, eviction-rate, p99 latency. Rollback threshold: p99 increase > 10% or eviction-rate +30% vs baseline.
2026-03-12 - Marco: Updating acceptance criteria to require telemetry and canary auto-rollback gates. Assigned estimate=8 to cover prototype->canary->observability fixes.
comments: Aditi (2026-03-04): We should keep canonicalization rules conservative initially (only whitespace, placeholder normalization, and a curated list of synonyms). Avoid early use of heavy semantic hashing.
Marco (2026-03-06): Agree. Prototype will export detailed logs of split points so we can refine heuristics before applying to live traffic.
Sana (2026-03-07): UX ask: Console should surface per-route anchor hit-rate so customers can understand cost savings. Add as a telemetry requirement.
Ethan (2026-03-09): Security: per-tenant salt introduced. Also recommend we treat fingerprint collisions as non-fatal: fallback to storing unmerged copies and emit an alert to telemetry.
Benji (2026-03-10): Test plans: include both short chat sessions (many small prefixes) and long-instruction pipelines. Will create replay trace subset for performance lab.
Marco (2026-03-12): PR #7312 in draft; allocator changes isolated under runtime feature flag. Next: run op-level stress with 64 GPUs in perf-cluster to validate compaction throttling heuristics.
